Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509

Class X509ForwardedHeadersGuard

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509.X509ForwardedHeadersGuard
public final class X509ForwardedHeadersGuard extends Object
Refuses to start when a certificate may be forwarded in a header while the server rewrites the address of its clients from the forwarded headers.

ForwardedCertificateFilter trusts a forwarded certificate only from the addresses of authserver.x509.trusted-proxies, and it reads the address with getRemoteAddr(), which is the address left once Spring Boot's forwarded-header handling has run. With server.forward-headers-strategy=framework, Spring's ForwardedHeaderFilter replaces it with the first value of X-Forwarded-For (or Forwarded), which any client can send: naming a trusted proxy there would make a forged certificate header look trusted. With native, Tomcat's RemoteIpValve replaces it with the client the proxies report, so the address of the proxy itself is never seen and the check is made against an address that came from a header. The same happens without the property on a cloud platform that Spring Boot detects, where native is the default. Only with none is the address the direct network peer, which no header can change, so that is the one combination allowed. The proxy is still free to send X-Forwarded-* headers; they are just not used.
